name: only_allowed_chars
rationale: Canonical morphemes are spelled with letters, plus any punctuation the word itself has, so every correct output passes. This rejects outputs containing digits, spaces or stray symbols.

name: no_whitespace_in_segments
rationale: A morpheme never contains whitespace unless the word does. This rejects explanations or prose leaking into segments.

name: lowercase_if_surface_lowercase
rationale: Gold morphemes for a lowercase word are themselves lowercase. This rejects outputs with spurious capitalisation.

name: seg_count_le_length
rationale: There cannot be more morphemes than letters in the word. This catches degenerate, over-split outputs.

name: first_char_matches
rationale: Canonical restoration changes stem endings, not the first letter of the word. This catches outputs whose first segment is unrelated to the word.

name: total_length_bounded
rationale: Canonical forms add only a few letters per boundary. This catches wildly bloated or hallucinated outputs.

name: total_length_lower_bound
rationale: Canonicalisation rarely removes more than a few letters. This catches truncated outputs.

name: segment_not_too_long
rationale: No single morpheme greatly exceeds the length of the whole word. This catches run-on segments.

name: similarity_to_surface
rationale: The joined morphemes stay very close to the surface string. This catches outputs that segment a different word.

name: single_segment_equals_surface
rationale: A word left unsegmented is its own canonical morpheme. This catches altered single-morpheme outputs.

name: no_digits_unless_surface
rationale: Digits cannot appear in morphemes unless the word contains them. This catches numbering artefacts such as "1. mis".

name: no_quotes_unless_surface
rationale: Quote characters belong in a morpheme only when the word itself contains them. This catches quoted output formatting.

name: each_seg_shares_letter
rationale: Every real morpheme overlaps the word's letters. Even inserted canonical vowels like 'y' or 'e' usually appear in the word. This catches junk segments.

name: first_seg_prefix_match
rationale: The first morpheme's opening letters copy the word's start. This catches misaligned first segments.

name: no_markdown
rationale: Markdown characters never occur in morphemes. This catches formatting leakage.

name: no_arrow
rationale: Arrows and equals signs are explanation syntax, not morpheme content. This catches outputs like "word -> ...".

name: seg_count_reasonable
rationale: English words have at most about one morpheme per two letters. This catches character-level splits.

name: no_all_single_letters
rationale: A correct segmentation of a long word is never all one-letter pieces. This catches spelled-out outputs.

name: no_surface_repeat
rationale: The full word never appears in its own segmentation alongside other morphemes. This catches outputs like "word+s" for "word".

name: ascii_if_surface_ascii
rationale: For an ASCII word, the canonical morphemes are ASCII. This catches encoding artefacts and odd glyphs.

name: no_internal_hyphen_unless_surface
rationale: A hyphen inside a morpheme is valid only if the word has one. This catches outputs that use '-' as the separator.

name: no_slash
rationale: A slash marks alternative answers, which are never part of the gold. This catches hedged outputs.

name: no_comma_semicolon
rationale: Commas, semicolons and colons are list or explanation punctuation, not morphemes. This catches outputs that use them as separators.

name: no_period
rationale: A full stop inside segments is sentence punctuation, unless the word contains one. This catches trailing-period outputs.

name: letters_coverage
rationale: Most of the word's letters must reappear in the morphemes, since canonicalisation edits only boundaries. This catches outputs that drop large chunks of the word.
